The Midnight, Endless Summer (album cover)

The cover of The Midnight’s first album: a glowing pink neon script over a star-speckled figure, with VHS tracking noise and an on-screen play label.

Source
The Midnight Wiki: Endless Summer
Creator
Taylor Allen
Made
Released 5 August 2016 (The Midnight Wiki; Discogs)
Style
Synthwave (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Nostalgic, nocturnal, romantic
Evidence
Inspected the 1200 px front-cover image from the Cover Art Archive in a scratch folder. Not stored. The artist credit comes from The Midnight Wiki; the Discogs record of the 2016 digital release lists no artwork credit.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Midnight Wiki: Endless Summer is the band’s first album, released independently on 5 August 2016. “A small snip of the album artwork (done by Taylor Allen) was revealed in July,” and the full artwork was revealed with the announcement on 25 July. The Midnight Wiki.

Discogs records the original release as a self-released digital file of 5 August 2016, written by Tim McEwan and Tyler Lyle. Discogs.

Observed

  • The ground is near-black, crossed by faint horizontal lines of video noise. Two bands of heavier static run across the lower third.
  • A tilted female figure, filled with a star field in cyan, blue, violet, and magenta, rises through the centre.
  • “The Midnight” crosses the figure in a monoline script drawn as a pink neon tube: a white-hot core, a magenta glow, and a thin cyan and yellow colour offset.
  • Below, “▶ ENDLESS SUMMER” and “©1984” are set in small, light, pixel-like capitals, like a VCR on-screen display, with a red and cyan colour fringe.

Why it belongs

The cover shows that VHS artefacts in synthwave are an accent of memory, not decay: the image stays sharp and saturated, and the noise sits on top of it. The false “©1984” date sets the scene in an imagined past.

Borrow

Draw a script logotype as a neon tube: a white core line, a wide magenta glow, and a one-pixel cyan offset.

Label a section like a VCR display: a play triangle and small pixel capitals.
